# Data center commissioning QA

Research notes. Leyoxa is exploring AI-assisted commissioning QA; it is not yet a commercial offering. The pages below describe the approach being researched.

AI halls are energized on compressed schedules by stretched electrical crews. Leyoxa Verify produces evidence for every connection before energization and watches it under load. Qualified engineers make every acceptance decision.

## Where it helps

- **Before energization (Levels 2–3).** Switchgear, busway, UPS, PDUs and RPPs: every label checked against the one-line diagram, every lug checked for its torque mark and matched to its torque record.
- **Test results.** Insulation resistance, contact resistance, breaker and relay tests read from the test sets and checked against NETA acceptance limits, with outliers flagged even when they pass.
- **Under load (Levels 4–5).** Thermal scans during load-bank testing and integrated systems testing catch the joint running hotter than its neighbours.
- **Handover.** Findings with photos, locations and the standard they cite, closed on an iPhone and collected into the turnover package.

## Why now

A one-month delay can cost up to $14.2M on a typical 60 MW data center ([STL Partners, 2025](https://stlpartners.com/press/delays-in-data-centre-construction/)), and across 25 million sq ft of 2025 data center builds, electrical containment went in at 59.4% of the required pace ([Buildots](https://buildots.com/lab/data-center-mep-benchmarks/)). Crews are short; the checks are not optional.

## On a live site

- **Humans accept.** Verify supplies evidence and flags anomalies; your engineers decide.
- **Safe by design.** Visual checks on de-energized gear; thermal under load through IR windows or with qualified staff, per NFPA 70E.
- **Imagery stays on site.** Edge processing; nothing leaves unless you export it.

If you build or commission electrical systems and want to compare notes, write to [contact@leyoxa.com](mailto:contact@leyoxa.com?subject=Commissioning%20QA%20research).

# Energy commissioning QA

Research notes. Leyoxa is exploring AI-assisted commissioning QA; it is not yet a commercial offering. The pages below describe the approach being researched.

*Leyoxa Verify starts with AI data centers. The same checks apply here, and this is where we go next.*

Solar, battery storage, substations and on-site power all end the same way: thousands of connections that have to be right before the system is energized. Leyoxa Verify checks them, reads the test results, and writes the handover.

## Where it helps

- **Battery storage.** Busbar joints, DC and AC wiring and auxiliary systems checked before energization, then watched under the first charge and discharge cycles.
- **Solar.** String test results and IV curves read across the whole plant, with the string that passes but underperforms its peers flagged, checked against IEC 62446 limits.
- **Substations and switchyards.** Terminations, labels and relay and breaker test results checked against the design, with thermal scans under first load.
- **On-site power for data centers.** Switchgear, transformers and generator connections verified before the facility depends on them.

## Why now

In EPRI’s database of battery storage failures, 72% of failures with a known system age happened during construction, commissioning or the first two years of operation, and most traced to build quality in wiring, cooling and safety systems ([EPRI with TWAICE and PNNL, 2024](https://www.powermag.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/bess-failure-report.pdf)). The cheapest place to catch them is before energization.

## On a live site

- **Alongside your crew.** It captures, checks and documents; your testers decide.
- **Safe by design.** Per NFPA 70E, with thermal under load through IR windows or with qualified staff.
- **Built for big yards.** On a cart or in a technician’s hand first; a robot for repeated sweeps across large outdoor sites.

If you build or commission electrical systems and want to compare notes, write to [contact@leyoxa.com](mailto:contact@leyoxa.com?subject=Commissioning%20QA%20research).

# Questions

Research notes. Leyoxa is exploring AI-assisted commissioning QA; it is not yet a commercial offering. The pages below describe the approach being researched.

### What is Leyoxa Verify?
AI commissioning QA for data center electrical systems. It reads every test result, checks every termination and label against the design, catches hot joints under first load, and writes the handover package, so there is evidence for every connection before energization.

### Does Verify accept or approve equipment?
No. Verify supplies evidence and flags anomalies. Qualified engineers make every acceptance decision, and “no anomaly flagged” never means “accepted”.

### Does it replace our testing technicians?
No. It works alongside your NETA or commissioning crew: it captures, checks and documents, so each technician covers more equipment and nothing is missed.

### Is it safe around energized equipment?
It follows the same rules your crew does. Visual inspection happens on de-energized gear with covers off; thermal scans under load go through IR windows or with qualified staff present, per NFPA 70E.

### Do we need a robot?
No. Verify starts on a cart or in a technician’s hand. A robot pays off for repeated sweeps during first load and on large outdoor yards.

### Which standards does it check against?
Your project specifications first, then the acceptance standards they call on, such as ANSI/NETA ATS for electrical equipment and IEC 62446 for solar.

### Which builds does it work on?
We start with AI data centers. The same checks apply to battery storage, substations, on-site power, fabs and battery plants, and those come next.

### Does a torque mark prove a bolt was torqued?
No. A mark is evidence that someone marked it. Verify matches each mark to its torque record and flags marks with no record and records with no mark.

### Where does site imagery go?
It stays on site by default. Processing runs on edge hardware, with exports only to the commissioning platform you choose.

### What does a pilot look like?
One electrical room, about 8 to 12 weeks, in parallel with your crew. It is measured on recall against validated defects, precision, what the crew missed, and time per asset to a verified close. Scope and price are agreed up front.

### Who builds it?
Leyoxa LLC was founded by [Sepehr Aflatounian](https://sepehrafla.github.io), a University of Waterloo computer engineer who led its autonomous driving team, co-founded a machine-learning startup for cyber-attack detection, and built sign-in for millions of banking customers.

### Where do you work?
The United States, Canada and the Middle East.

### How do we start?
Email [contact@leyoxa.com](mailto:contact@leyoxa.com?subject=Pilot) with the build, the country and your commissioning dates.

# How it works

Research notes. Leyoxa is exploring AI-assisted commissioning QA; it is not yet a commercial offering. The pages below describe the approach being researched.

Leyoxa Verify produces evidence for every electrical connection before an AI data center is energized: it reads every test result, checks what was installed against the design, and writes the handover. **Verify supplies evidence and flags anomalies. Qualified engineers make every acceptance decision.**

## 1. Test

Verify reads the results your crew already produces and checks them against the acceptance limits:

| Test | What Verify looks for |
|---|---|
| Insulation resistance | Readings below limit, and readings far below their peers |
| Contact and winding resistance | Imbalance between phases |
| Breaker and relay tests | Settings that do not match the coordination study |
| Solar IV curves | Strings that pass but underperform their neighbours |
| Load-bank and first-load thermal | Joints running hotter than the same joint on other phases |

## 2. Inspect

Before energization, Verify walks the electrical rooms, yards and substations, on a robot, a cart or in a technician’s hand. RGB, thermal and depth sensors capture every compartment. Computer vision checks:

- every label against the one-line diagram and panel schedules
- every lug for its torque mark, matched to its torque record (a mark is evidence that someone marked the bolt; the record is what counts)
- cable routing and segregation against the design

## 3. Hand over

Every finding gets a photo, a location and the standard it cites, and goes to the technician’s iPhone. It is closed with a photo and a rescan, and the evidence is collected into the turnover package for your commissioning platform.

## The pilot

- **Scope.** One electrical room, battery yard or substation, during commissioning. Scope and price agreed before we start.
- **Duration.** About 8 to 12 weeks.
- **Method.** Verify runs in parallel with your crew’s own inspection and IR survey. Nothing in your process changes.
- **Measured.** Recall against the validated defects, precision (how many flags were real), what Verify found that the crew missed, inspection and documentation time per asset, and time from finding to verified close.

## Safety and data

- **Humans accept.** Verify supplies evidence and flags anomalies; qualified engineers make every acceptance decision.
- **Safe by design.** Visual inspection on de-energized gear with covers off; thermal under load through IR windows or with qualified staff present, per NFPA 70E.
- **Imagery stays on site.** Processing on edge hardware; exports only to the platform you choose.

Start with an email to [contact@leyoxa.com](mailto:contact@leyoxa.com?subject=Pilot): the build, the country and your commissioning dates.

# Leyoxa

> Leyoxa designs, builds and runs production AI systems for real-world operations, where mistakes cost money: agents that work inside the software a business already uses, live, every day.

## What we build

- **Production AI agents.** Voice and workflow agents that answer live calls, book, follow up and hand off to a person when it matters, judged by what they actually did.
- **Integrations.** Agents that read and write the software a business already depends on, including old and messy systems.
- **Data and reporting.** Pipelines that turn operational data into numbers people trust.
- **Security and privacy.** Identity, access and data handling designed in from the start, including regulated and sensitive information.

## Research

AI-assisted commissioning QA for electrical systems on data center and energy builds: reading test results against limits and peers, checking terminations against the drawings, and catching hot joints under first load. A research area, not yet a commercial offering. [Research notes](https://leyoxa.com/how-it-works.md).

## Who builds it

Toronto · Austin · contact@leyoxa.com

# Manufacturing commissioning QA

Research notes. Leyoxa is exploring AI-assisted commissioning QA; it is not yet a commercial offering. The pages below describe the approach being researched.

*Leyoxa Verify starts with AI data centers. The same checks apply here, and this is where we go next.*

New fabs, battery plants and gigafactories energize thousands of panels and feeders on schedules that cannot slip. Leyoxa Verify checks each one against the design and documents it, so the plant starts on time and stays up.

## Where it helps

- **Distribution and panels.** Labels, terminations and torque marks checked against the one-line diagram and panel schedules.
- **Test results.** Insulation and contact resistance and breaker tests read and checked against acceptance limits, outliers flagged.
- **First load.** Thermal scans as production equipment comes online catch the connection running hot.
- **Handover.** Every finding documented with a photo, location and the standard it cites.

## On a live site

- **Alongside your crew**, with every decision staying with your testers.
- **Safe by design**, per NFPA 70E.
- **Imagery stays on site**, which matters in plants with strict confidentiality rules.

If you build or commission electrical systems and want to compare notes, write to [contact@leyoxa.com](mailto:contact@leyoxa.com?subject=Commissioning%20QA%20research).
